transcript.text: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. As you know, there's been recurring tension during handoffs on the product-operations team, and several team members have suggested trying a peer repair circle. Before I approve the program and finalize its operating terms, I want to gather input from each of you and from People Operations as part of our normal review process for team-support initiatives. I'd love to hear your thoughts -- any concerns, hopes, or conditions you'd want to see addressed. Let's start with whatever's top of mind for you.

transcript.text: I want to raise a concern about Lee being the facilitator. I've personally observed Lee interrupting and dismissing colleagues in three recent repair discussions. I'm worried that participants won't feel safe speaking freely if Lee facilitates the circle. I haven't put these observations into a formal feedback record, but I felt it was important to share now before the plan is finalized.

transcript.text: I want to flag a scheduling constraint. I have a standing caregiving commitment on Wednesday evenings, so I can only reliably attend on Tuesdays from 16:00 to 17:00. I've already told the program's organizer that this is the time I could sustain for the full trial. I want to make sure this is taken into account before the schedule is finalized.

transcript.text: I need to share some important People Operations policy findings before this plan is finalized. I completed my policy check this week, and there are three requirements that apply: first, participation in a peer repair circle must be strictly opt-in; second, any disclosures made within the circle are prohibited from being used in performance evaluations; and third, an initial trial is limited to exactly six weeks. I understand the draft plan was circulated before I finished this check, so these terms may not yet be reflected in it. I'd recommend Helena incorporate these as non-negotiable operating terms before giving final approval.

transcript.text:
Thank you all for this valuable input. Let me address each point:

Darius, thank you for raising that concern about Lee. That's exactly the kind of information I need before finalizing. If Lee has been observed interrupting and dismissing colleagues in repair discussions, that's a serious consideration for a facilitator role where psychological safety is paramount. I'll need to weigh this carefully.

Mei, thank you for flagging the scheduling constraint. Tuesday 16:00-17:00 seems like it could work, and I want to make sure the chosen time is sustainable for all participants.

Rafael, thank you for the People Operations policy findings. Those three requirements -- strictly opt-in participation, confidentiality of disclosures from performance evaluations, and a six-week trial limit -- will absolutely be incorporated as non-negotiable operating terms.

Given what I've heard, I have some thinking to do. The facilitator concern is significant enough that I may need to explore alternatives to Lee before approving. Let me consider all of this and come back with a decision shortly.
